subject: Draft rate-letter & throughput SLO for renewal
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@wavehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Draft rate-letter & throughput SLO for renewal

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion I attached a draft rate-letter and an SLO exhibits spreadsheet that captures the reserved pool increase you requested for the renewal. High level summary below so procurement has something concise to review: 

- Term: 24 months (renewal effective 2027-01-01)
- Reserved capacity: add four (4) rA100-equivalent GPUs to current pool (total reserved = 12 GPUs)
- Throughput ladder: guaranteed baseline 280k tokens/sec across the reserved pool, burst to 420k tokens/sec under burst windows described in Exhibit B
- SLO & credits: monthly SLO measured at the pool-level. If monthly achieved throughput < 95% of the guaranteed baseline, credit = max(1%, (95% - achieved%) * 1.5%) of that month's reserved fee; see Exhibit C for full formula
- Latency guardrail: 95th percentile request latency target of 280ms for 1k-token seq on the pinned model; automatic fallback to a quantized model variant with documented quality delta when latency SLO is at risk
- Pricing: incremental GPU-rate + token-rate discount per the attached rate-letter (illustrative scenarios on tab 2 of SLO-exhibits.xlsx)

I've purposefully left legal language at a high level in the draft — Ben, Marissa: can you review the credit formula and fallback language and flag anything procurement/legal will push back on?

Liam / Sophie: would you and procurement prefer we file the SLO as an addendum to the existing MSA or include it inline in the renewal amendment? Either is fine from our side but procurement signatures differ depending on the choice.

Next steps I propose:
- You review this week and indicate preferred contract vehicle (addendum vs inline)
- We schedule a 30-min alignment call (I can bring our SRE) to walk the SLO measurement and rollback/fallback behavior
- If procurement ok, send final rate-letter for legal redline by 2026-11-20 to keep current pricing windows

Thanks —

Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
m: (415) 555-0142
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: 20261114-rate-letter-draft.pdf; SLO-exhibits.xlsx; SOW-appendix-A.docx

From: Sophie Li <sophie.li@wavehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@wavehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@wavehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-15T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft rate-letter & throughput SLO for renewal

Thanks Monica — quick clarifying Qs from procurement/security before we loop legal:

1) Measurement window: is the SLO measured on UTC months or our billing month (we use the first-to-last day local for billing)?
2) Auditability: will Redwood provide monthly measurement reports and per-request traces on demand for up to 6 months? We need this for our internal audit.
3) Data residency: does the fallback path (quantized model variant) ever route inference to a non-US region? We must ensure all inference for WaveHealth stays in the us region.

Also, Sophie (procurement): the credit formula sounds fine but we need a cap so credits don't compound in a multi-month outage. Recommend a per-event cap equal to 25% of the monthly fee.

Happy to review the SLO-exhibits live — can you hold a call Friday 11/19 09:30 PT?

—Sophie
Sophie Li
Sr. Manager, Procurement | WaveHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@wavehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@wavehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft rate-letter & throughput SLO for renewal

Sophie — thanks for the concrete asks, good catches. A couple notes from our side: 

- Measurement window: we measure SLOs on UTC months by default but we can align billing vs measurement in contract language; propose "SLO measurement period aligns to the billing period as defined in Exhibit A" to avoid mismatch.
- Auditability: yes — monthly SLO reports plus a limited request-level audit export (traces + aggregated metrics) available on request for up to 12 weeks; if WaveHealth needs a longer retention window we can add an add-on.
- Data residency: confirmed — reserved pool for WaveHealth will be pinned to the us-east region and fallback variants will execute in the same region; we'll include a regional routing clause and a verification runbook.
- Credit cap: agreeable to a per-event cap (25% monthly fee). We also propose an annual cap of 50% of one month's reserved fee for cumulative credits in a 12-month rolling window to keep commercial exposure bounded.

Monica / Marissa: the legal redline items I expect we'll need to answer: exact monitoring endpoints, the definition of "achieved throughput" (pool-level tokens/sec averaged over 10-minute buckets? aggregated over the month?), and the rollback policy that triggers fallback to the quantized variant. I've sketched suggested language in the attached SLO-exhibits.xlsx (tab named 'Contract language').

I can join the Friday call from 09:20 PT to walk the measurement math.

Ben Carter
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@wavehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Li <sophie.li@wavehealth.com>, procurement@wavehealth.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft rate-letter & throughput SLO for renewal

Monica / Ben — appreciate the rapid follow-ups and the level of detail. WaveHealth preference is:

- Put the SLO in an addendum to the MSA (simpler for our internal routing)
- Measurement period should align to our billing period — please use the clause you proposed
- Credit cap: per-event cap 25% ok; annual cap sounds reasonable
- Data residency: confirm the US-only routing and include a verification runbook as Ben suggested

We can do the 11/19 09:30 PT call — please send a calendar invite and an agenda (30 min). After that call procurement legal will aim to provide redlines within 5 business days. If all looks good we'll route for signature and target effective date 2027-01-01.

Also quick ask: can you include an operations onboarding checklist in the SOW appendix (key contacts, monitoring endpoints, escalation path, DR test window)? That will help our SRE team sign off.

Thanks —
Liam O'Connor
Director of ML Platform | WaveHealth
liam.oconnor@wavehealth.com
